contentEn:
Thousands of homes across Vancouver and the rest of BC contain a hidden plumbing time bomb: polybutylene (Poly-B) piping. This cheap, gray or blue plastic pipe was installed in an estimated 3 to 4 million Canadian homes between 1980 and 1998, and it is still inside thousands of Metro Vancouver properties today. When Poly-B fails, it fails fast — no warning, significant water damage, and costs that dwarf what preventive replacement would have cost. If you own or are buying a Vancouver home built in that era, here is what you need to know in 2026.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Is It a Problem?

Polybutylene (Poly-B) is a plastic resin pipe manufactured from approximately 1978 through to the late 1990s. It was sold as an affordable alternative to copper for residential water supply lines and was widely used in Canadian construction throughout the 1980s and into the 1990s. The pipes are typically gray, black, or blue-white in color and often stamped with markings like "PB2110."

The problem: Poly-B degrades when exposed to oxidants commonly found in municipal water supplies, including chlorine. Over 15 to 20 years, the pipe's inner walls become brittle, scale builds up, and micro-cracks develop. The pipe can then fail catastrophically — a joint lets go or the pipe splits — typically at connection points and fitting joints. The Canadian boil water advisory that affected over 100,000 residents in Kaslo, BC in 2022 was linked to aging infrastructure including Poly-B failures, illustrating the real-world consequences of deferred pipe replacement.

Home insurance is increasingly a concern. Several Canadian insurers now decline to cover homes with documented Poly-B piping, or they add expensive exclusions. When you sell a BC home, the Property Disclosure Statement requires you to disclose the presence of Poly-B — and savvy buyers in 2026 are walking away or demanding the replacement be completed before closing.

Poly-B Pipe Replacement Cost in Vancouver and BC (2026)

Full re-piping of a Vancouver or Metro BC home in 2026 costs between $3,500 and $15,000, depending on the size of the home, the number of fixtures, and the material chosen. Here are typical installed price ranges:

  • PEX tubing (cross-linked polyethylene): $3,500 – $8,000 for an average single-family home. PEX is flexible, freeze-resistant, and the most common modern replacement. PEX-a offers the highest durability.
  • Copper re-pipe: $8,000 – $15,000 for an average single-family home. Copper is the premium option — it lasts 50+ years, handles high water pressure, and some buyers and insurers prefer it. Higher material and labor cost.
  • PEX-a with manifold (centralized distribution): $10,000 – $15,000+. Each fixture gets its own dedicated line from a central manifold — eliminating nearly all fittings inside walls. Best performance, highest cost.

A planned replacement during a renovation project is significantly cheaper than emergency repair. Tearing out walls for a kitchen or bathroom renovation anyway means plumbing is already exposed — adding re-piping at that point typically adds $1,500 to $4,000 to the overall project cost. Compare that to $8,000 to $25,000 for emergency re-piping through finished walls.

BC Real Estate Disclosure Rules for Poly-B (2026)

BC homeowners selling a property must complete a Property Disclosure Statement (PDS) before closing. The PDS includes a question about whether the home has Poly-B piping — sellers must answer truthfully. Failure to disclose is grounds for post-sale legal claims.

For buyers: a home inspection that identifies Poly-B should trigger a renegotiation of price or a seller credit for the replacement cost. In Vancouver's competitive market, some buyers are accepting the risk — but they are doing so with eyes open about the $3,500 to $15,000 expense that awaits them.

For Reno Stars clients in Richmond, Burnaby, Surrey, and across Metro Vancouver, the recommendation is consistent: if your home has Poly-B and you are planning any renovation that opens walls, re-pipe at the same time. The marginal cost is modest compared to doing it later, and it eliminates a material disclosure obligation on future sale.

When to Replace Poly-B: Now or Later?

The case for replacing Poly-B now is strongest when walls are already open. If you are renovating a kitchen, bathroom, or basement in a Vancouver home built between 1980 and 1998, adding re-piping to the scope is the most cost-effective time to address it. Reno Stars has completed whole-house renovation projects in Vancouver, Richmond, and Burnaby where Poly-B re-piping was included in the scope — homeowners avoided a future standalone plumbing emergency.

Waiting is only reasonable if a plumber has assessed the system and confirmed it is in good condition with no visible signs of degradation — and even then, replacement within five years is advisable given the age of the pipe.

Do You Need a Permit for Poly-B Re-piping in Vancouver?

Yes. Re-piping a Vancouver home requires a plumbing permit from the City of Vancouver (or the relevant municipality for other Metro BC cities). A qualified plumber pulls the permit and arranges the required inspections. The permit process typically adds $200 to $500 to the total project cost and 1 to 2 weeks to the schedule. Reno Stars coordinates all permit applications as part of our renovation projects.

How do I know if my Vancouver home has Poly-B pipes?

Poly-B pipes are typically gray, black, or blue-white plastic pipes found at the main water shutoff, at fixture connections, or visible in basements and mechanical rooms. Look for stamped markings such as "PB2110" or "Polybutylene." A licensed plumber can confirm in 30 minutes for a small inspection fee.

Is Poly-B pipe covered by home insurance in BC?

Coverage varies by insurer. Some BC insurers will cover a home with Poly-B if a licensed plumber's report confirms good condition. Others decline coverage or add exclusions. The safest position is to replace the pipe before renewal or purchase.

How long does Poly-B pipe last before it fails?

Poly-B pipes typically degrade over 15 to 25 years from installation. A home built in 1990 could begin experiencing failures any time from 2005 onward. Failures are most common at joints and fittings, not along straight runs of pipe.

Can I replace just the bad sections of Poly-B pipe?

Patching is possible in the short term but is not recommended as a permanent solution. Each joint is a potential failure point, and the underlying degradation of the remaining pipe continues. Full re-piping with PEX or copper is the standard professional recommendation.

What is the cost to repipe a Vancouver townhouse vs. a single-family home?

A townhouse or condo with shared walls typically costs $2,500 to $6,000 to re-pipe because there are fewer supply runs. A detached single-family home with more lineal feet of pipe and more fixture connections runs $3,500 to $15,000 depending on material choice and complexity.

聚丁烯（Poly-B）管道在大温及BC省是一场随时可能爆发的漏水道危机。1980年至1998年间，约300至400万套加拿大住宅安装了这种廉价塑料水管，其中数千套仍位于大温地区。Poly-B爆裂前毫无预兆，一旦破裂将造成重大水损，更换成本也远高于预防性更换。如果您拥有或购买1980年代至1998年间建成的温哥华住宅，2026年需要了解以下关键信息。

计划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？获取Reno Stars的免费、无压力报价。

什么是Poly-B管道，为什么是个问题？

聚丁烯（Poly-B）是一种塑料树脂管，大约从1978年至1990年代末期生产，曾作为铜管的廉价替代品广泛应用于加拿大的住宅供水管道。管道通常为灰色、黑色或蓝白色，并印有"PB2110"等标记。

问题根源：Poly-B接触市政供水中常见的氧化剂（包括氯）后会降解。经过15至20年，管道内壁变脆、结垢、微裂缝扩展。管道可能在接头处突然爆裂或裂开。2022年BC省Kaslo超过10万居民的煮沸水警报与包括Poly-B管道老化在内的基础设施问题直接相关，印证了推迟管道更换的现实后果。

房屋保险也越来越成问题。多加加拿大保险公司现在拒绝为有已确认Poly-B管道的房屋投保，或附加昂贵的除外条款。在BC省出售房屋时，必须在房产披露声明中申报Poly-B——2026年精明的买家正在因此要求在交割前完成更换，或直接放弃交易。

温哥华及BC省Poly-B管道更换费用（2026年）

2026年大温或Metro BC住宅全屋重铺管道的费用为$3,500至$15,000，取决于房屋面积、卫浴数量和所选材料。以下是各方案的典型安装价格范围：

  • PEX管道（交联聚乙烯）：普通独立屋$3,500至$8,000。PEX柔软、抗冻，是最常见的现代替代方案。PEX-a耐用性最高。
  • 铜管重铺：普通独立屋$8,000至$15,000。铜管是高端选择——使用寿命50年以上，耐高压，一些买家和保险公司更倾向铜管。材料和人工成本较高。
  • PEX-a集中分水系统：$10,000至$15,000以上。每个卫浴设备都有独立管道从中央分水器直达——几乎消除了墙内所有接头。性能最佳，成本最高。

在装修期间进行计划性更换，比紧急维修便宜得多。厨房或浴室装修本来就要打开墙体——此时同步重铺管道，通常只需增加$1,500至$4,000。相比已完成装修的墙体进行紧急重铺费用为$8,000至$25,000，差别显著。

BC省Poly-B房地产披露规定（2026年）

BC省卖家在交割前必须填写房产披露声明（Property Disclosure Statement, PDS）。PDS包含一项关于房屋是否有Poly-B管道的问题——卖家必须如实回答。隐瞒可构成交割后诉讼理由。

对于买家：房屋检查发现Poly-B后，应重新谈判价格或要求卖家提供更换费用的信用额度。在2026年竞争激烈的大温市场，一些买家选择接受风险——但他们清楚地知道即将面临的$3,500至$15,000支出。

对于Reno Stars在列治文、本拿比、素里及大温各地的客户，建议一致：如果您的房屋有Poly-B，且正计划任何需要打开墙体的装修，请同步重铺管道。相比未来单独进行紧急重铺，额外成本微乎其微，同时消除了未来出售时的材料披露义务。

何时更换Poly-B：现在还是将来？

更换Poly-B的最佳时机是墙体已经打开时。如果您在装修1980至1998年间建成的温哥华住宅的厨房、浴室或地下室，将重铺管道纳入工程范围是解决此问题最具成本效益的方式。Reno Stars在温哥华、列治文和本拿比完成的多个全屋装修项目中，都将Poly-B重铺纳入工程范围——业主因此避免了未来的单独紧急管道维修。

只有在水管工评估系统并确认状况良好且无明显降解迹象时，等待才是合理的——即便如此，考虑到管道年龄，五年内更换仍是明智建议。

温哥华Poly-B重铺需要许可吗？

需要。重铺温哥华住宅管道需要从温哥华市政府（或Metro BC其他相关城市政府）申请管道许可。持牌水管工提交许可申请并安排必要检查。许可流程通常增加$200至$500的总体成本，以及1至2周的工期。Reno Stars在装修项目中协调所有许可申请。

如何判断我的温哥华住宅是否有Poly-B管道？

Poly-B管道通常为灰色、黑色或蓝白色塑料管，位于主进水阀、卫浴设备连接处，或地下室和机房可见。寻找"PB2110"或"Polybutylene"等印字。持牌水管工可在30分钟内确认，费用很低。

BC省Poly-B管道在房屋保险覆盖范围内吗？

保险覆盖因保险公司而异。部分BC省保险公司在持牌水管工报告确认状况良好后可为有Poly-B的房屋承保。其他公司则拒绝承保或附加除外条款。最安全的做法是在续保或购房前更换管道。

Poly-B管道在多久后开始出问题？

Poly-B管道通常在安装后15至25年内降解。1990年建成的房屋可能从2005年起随时出现故障。故障最常见于接头处，而非管道直段。

我能否只更换Poly-B的损坏部分？

短期补丁修补可行，但不推荐作为永久解决方案。每个接头都是潜在故障点，剩余管道的持续降解仍在进行中。全屋重铺PEX或铜管是专业标准建议。
